newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner holds option on Bergesen shares.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner holds option on Bergesen shares.

text.p: Anglo-Norwegian construction group Kvaerner ASA has sold its stake in Norway's largest shipping company Bergesen ASA, but retains its economic exposure to Bergesen's share price via a call and put option, Kvaerner said on Monday.

Kvaerner sold its 17.06 percent stake of Bergesen A shares and 17.06 percent of B stock to SBC Warburg. But, it said, it had entered a call and put option with Warburg under which Kvaerner may at any time until maturity buy back the shares.
Under the same agreement, Warburg may sell the shares back to Kvaerner, if Kvaerner has not exercised its right under the call option.
"The option agreement allows Kvaerner to sustain its economic exposure to Bergesen's share price," Kvaerner said in a statement.
Svein Erik Amundsen, executive vice president in Bergesen said the sale had been expected. But as long as the option agreement exists -- 12 months, Bergesen considers Kvaerner as a major shareholder.
"We will have to come back to this when the option has run out in 12 months but until then we see Kvaerner as the real owner," Amundsen told Reuters.

Kvaerner had previously announced that it intended to sell its Bergesen stake as part of a 10 billion crown asset sale programme following the acquisition of British conglomerate Trafalgar House Plc last year.
